latest_release.name: Mac.apk v1.0.2379 (alpha)
latest_release.body:
## Mac.apk v1.0.2379 (alpha)

A small patch release: installing apps from F-Droid works again.

**Requires** macOS 26.4 (Tahoe) or later on Apple Silicon. macOS 27 is supported.

**The first launch of each app after you update is slower, once.** Mac.apk rebuilds each app's converted code and native translations for the new version, and every launch after that is back to normal speed.

### Fixed since v1.0.2377

- **F-Droid could not install apps.** The newer F-Droid asks for approval before it downloads, and Mac.apk answered that approval was not available, so every install stopped with "Error installing". It now gets the answer F-Droid expects. You still get the Touch ID prompt before anything is installed ([#139](https://github.com/kksimp/Mac.apk/issues/139)).

If you tap Install on several apps in F-Droid, the later ones show "waiting to start download" until the earlier downloads finish. That is F-Droid's own queue.

Thank you to @kengoon for reporting this ([#139](https://github.com/kksimp/Mac.apk/issues/139)).

### Install

Download `macapk.dmg`, open it, and drag Mac.apk to Applications (replace the old copy if you have one). The app is signed with a Developer ID and notarized by Apple.

Source code for the two LGPL libraries Mac.apk ships (GLib and GNU gettext's libintl) is attached below, with `LGPL-SOURCE-README.txt`; all third-party notices are in `THIRD_PARTY_NOTICES.txt` in the repository.

SHA-256 of `macapk.dmg`: `4ab633e6559a33a281b97aa19f249f8aae8fd177275890695658a6b2ab88bad2`
